comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Seen in real use, not only on a crash, 2026-09-28 upgrading 0.10.1 -> 0.11.0 on Alex's Mac. The 0.10.1 app was quit with a plain cmd-Q and its devenv ssh master outlived it: `ssh -N -M -S $TMPDIR/muster-35954-devenv.ctl ...`, started 12:43 by a reconnect during that app's life, reparented to launchd. Its forward kept the old window's socket (/home/.muster/daemon/window-w27br3drgx.sock) listening on the devenv, so `muster window` from a pane made by 0.10.1 exited 4, 'took the request and never answered (Connection reset by peer)', instead of reaching the 0.11 window as the 0.11.0 release notes say it now does. `ssh -O exit -S <that ctl> aterp-chco` fixed it at once: the old socket stopped listening and the same command answered from the new window. So a leaked master defeats the stale-window fallback, and a clean quit leaks one when the master was started by a reconnect.

creator: Alexander Terp
description: Found building the --ssh tier's handover test: a process that exits without dropping its ssh session leaves the ControlMaster running, which holds any pipeline reading its output open. The window resets its session before the test's cleanup now; Muster itself may leave masters behind on a crash.
title: An ssh master can outlive a process that exits without dropping its session
